title: ci-benchmark-flakiness-investigation-apr02-2026
body:
Summary:

This doc captures the observed flakiness on the CI benchmark runner for the nightly throughput/latency suite (linux-x86-gpu-03) over the last 10 days. Tests show non-deterministic spikes in 95th/99th latency on otherwise identical runs. The goal is to record reproducible steps, relevant logs, current hypotheses, and a short list of mitigations to prove or rule out each hypothesis.

Why this matters:
- Nightly CI benchmarks feed the perf dashboard and alerting for regressions; noisy baselines are blocking automated regression detection.
- Flaky runs slow down patch rollouts because triage time increases (we often rerun tests 3–5x).
- Some downstream decisioning (autoscale profiles, default batch sizes) come from these runs. We need confidence in the numbers.

Observed pattern (high level):
- Window: 2026-03-23 through 2026-04-02.
- Frequency: ~30% of nightly runs show a 50–180 ms increase in p95 latency when compared to the previous clean baseline (same commit).
- Affected metrics: p95 generation latency, p99 generation latency, tokens/s throughput for short-seq (64) workloads. p50 mostly stable.
- Runs that exhibit spikes often show a corresponding increase in CPU steal on the host and a rise in GPU memory fragmentation markers in the runtime logs.
- Not all commits show the problem even on the same host. Some runs reproduce locally on the same commit when triggered within 10–20 minutes of the original failing run timestamp.

Keys (representative) runs and ids:
- run-2026-03-24T04:12:21Z (clean baseline) — p95=110 ms, tokens/s=380
- run-2026-03-26T04:13:05Z (spike) — p95=290 ms, tokens/s=160
- run-2026-03-29T04:10:58Z (spike) — p95=320 ms, tokens/s=145
- run-2026-04-01T04:11:30Z (near clean but tail drift) — p95=140 ms, tokens/s=350

Where we looked already (short summary of evidence):
1) Hardware contention on runner host
- Collected top/htop snapshots and blocked processes logs from linux-x86-gpu-03. Evidence: intermittent high iowait and occasional CPU steal events co-occurring with spike runs.
- VM telemetry indicates background snapshot tasks (host-level backups) run at ~03:58 UTC but not consistently every night.

2) Docker container warmup and cgroup throttling
- Some failing runs include libc error noise during container startup; cgroup cpu quotas temporarily low due to host-level scheduler interactions.
- Reproduced a weak variant by running 10 consecutive job starts: cold-start p95 diverges when container creation overlaps with a host cron job.

3) Runtime-level memory fragmentation / allocation path
- Runtime logs show more frequent GPU memory allocation retries and small defragmentation passes on spike runs.
- Kernel scheduler reports occasional longer memcpy times on failing runs.

4) Queueing/batching heuristics
- When throughput drops, we sometimes see batching windows widen; this is symptomatic (effect) not necessarily cause.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Host-level maintenance/backups overlapping CI jobs cause temporary CPU and IO contention => p95 spike (high confidence)
- H2: Container cold-start race with backup triggers a momentary cgroup quota starvation => p95 spike (medium confidence)
- H3: GPU driver/kernel transient that increases memcpy latency, possibly due to fragmentation or host thermals => p95 spike (medium-low confidence)
- H4: Non-deterministic scheduler path in runtime when facing allocation failures => p95 spike (low confidence)

Immediate experiments to run (short-term, <72h):
- E1 (owner: Aisha) — Disable host backup window on linux-x86-gpu-03 for two consecutive nights and compare runs (control vs disabled). Record topology, run ids. Target completion: 2026-04-04.
- E2 (owner: Marco) — Add a pre-warm step to CI job: start runtime container 90s earlier and keep warm, then run benchmark. Compare cold-start vs pre-warm p95. Target completion: 2026-04-03.
- E3 (owner: Ravi) — Run repeated microbench memcpy latency probe on gpu-03 while running CI benchmark to correlate memcpy jitter with p95 spikes. Also capture nvidia-smi dmon logs. Target completion: 2026-04-04.
- E4 (owner: Leah) — Force cgroup cpu quota to max for the job (no CPU throttling) and re-run nightly suite. Target completion: 2026-04-05.

Longer-term experiments / engineering mitigations (next sprint):
- Add a CI job runner health-check that gates the perf run if host metrics (iowait/steal/gpu-mem-frag) exceed thresholds.
- Implement a lightweight in-job warmup (affects CI only) that pre-allocs KV cache and warms CUDA contexts to reduce cold-start variance.
- Investigate runtime allocator hook to reduce small-allocation retries under fragmentation (follow-up with research team).
- Evaluate moving perf runs to dedicated hosts with pinned tenants (dedicated perf hardware) to remove noisy neighbor risk.

Data artifacts and where to find them:
- Perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.ai/dash/serving-runtime/nightly-suite (trend charts and raw CSV export)
- Raw logs + trace bundles: s3://redwood-ci-logs/serving-runtime/nightly/2026-03-24/ and corresponding run folders (see linked_artifacts).
- Runner telemetry (CPU/iowait/steal/cron): https://infra.redwood.ai/hosts/linux-x86-gpu-03/metrics (grafana links embedded in Confluence page)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some nights with the backup job not show spikes? Is there a timing offset or reduced backup IO footprint that avoids impact?
- Are there firmware/driver versions correlated with the memcpy latency changes? (need cross-host driver matrix)
- What is the expected variance floor for this suite under ideal conditions? We need to quantify baseline noise to decide alert thresholds.

Action items (owners + deadlines):
- Aisha: disable host backup (test window) and report results by 2026-04-04.
- Marco: add + measure pre-warm container step in CI job, PR to infra repo by 2026-04-03.
- Ravi: run memcpy probe and attach dmon traces; present correlation graph in next sync (2026-04-06).
- Leah: change CI job to enforce higher cpu cgroup quota for nightly perf runs and capture results by 2026-04-05.
- All: update PERF-4321 with results + mark which hypotheses were ruled out. Owner: Leah.

Notes from quick adhoc reproductions (2026-04-02):
- Reproduced a p95 ~2.5x spike when simultaneously starting two benchmarking containers on the same host while a snapshot job ran.
- In one run, strace inside the container showed repeated small GPU allocation syscalls; stack traces point to allocator fallback in runtime v0.19.3.

Risks and fallback plan:
- Risk: Disabling backups on infra hosts may not be approved by infra ops for extended windows. Fallback: schedule perf runs to avoid backup window (nightly start offset).
- Risk: Warmup skews baseline in a way that hides real customer cold-start regressions. Fallback: maintain both cold and warmed baselines; tag warmed-run results clearly in dashboard.

Meeting attendees (2026-04-02 10:00 UTC ad-hoc): Leah Kim (notes), Marco Jimenez, Aisha Patel, Ravi Shah, Priya Desai (SRE consult).

Next sync: 2026-04-06 perf triage — aim to close 2 of the short-term experiments and decide on one long-term mitigation to start in the next sprint.

Appendix (quick commands used during investigation):
- docker run --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash perf-runner:latest - used to reproduce cold-start behavior
- python tools/benchmark/runner.py --suite nightly --repeat 3 --collect-traces --out run-<ts>
- scripts/gpu-mem-probe.sh --duration 600 --interval 1s (collects cudaMalloc/cudaFree timings)
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ci-logs/serving-runtime/nightly/ run-local --recursive

If you have other leads to try, add to this doc and ping the channel #perf-bench-sync.
